tools.name: check_connection
tools.description: Sends one request through the service from TrueProxies and reports the outcome and exit IP, to tell a proxy problem apart from a website refusing you. It counts as use of the service: it uses a little traffic and starts an unused free trial. Does not measure speed. Limited to a few checks a minute.

tools.name: generate_endpoints
tools.description: Builds proxy connection lines for a service with the chosen protocol, format, location targeting and session type: one line, or up to 50,000 sticky sessions with session sticky. Does not change the service. The output contains the proxy username and password, which let anyone who has them use the se

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Returns the TrueProxies account that owns the API key: account reference, email, role, status and billing details.

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description: Returns one invoice: status, amounts in cents, payment attempts and its service. Does not start a payment.

tools.name: get_live_traffic
tools.description: Returns live traffic for one service: download and upload speed in bits per second over the last ten seconds, traffic used today (UTC) and recent connection outcomes. last_activity_at shows how fresh the data is.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Returns one service: status, expiry, connection hosts and ports, capabilities (the targeting and session options it supports) and effective limits. Does not return the proxy password.

tools.name: get_traffic_used
tools.description: Returns traffic for one service, in bytes: bytes_out is downloaded and bytes_in is uploaded since the service started, remaining_bytes is traffic remaining and allowance_bytes is the allowance. traffic_batches lists traffic packs; traffic bought now never expires, and only older packs carry an expir

tools.name: get_usage_history
tools.description: Returns usage history for one service, or for the whole account when service_id is empty: connection success, traffic and connection errors over the last 24h, 7d or 30d. In series, bytes_out is downloaded and bytes_in is uploaded. Can lag recent traffic.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: Lists invoices with status (open, paid or cancelled), kind, amount in cents and the service each belongs to. Paginated: pass next_cursor from the previous response as cursor.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: Lists TrueProxies plans and traffic packs: price in US cents, term, speed, connection limits, traffic allowance and targeting capabilities. Also returns the cities available for city targeting and whether the free trial is open. Traffic packs (residential_ipv4_gb, residential_ipv4_premium, residenti

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Lists the services on the account with status, product, plan, expiry and connection hosts. Paginated: pass next_cursor from the previous response as cursor.

tools.name: list_trusted_ips
tools.description: Lists the IP whitelist of a service: addresses allowed to connect without the proxy password.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account · Private data: generate_endpoints, get_account, get_service, list_plans, list_trusted_ips · Public sink: get_account, get_live_traffic · Destructive: generate_endpoints.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account · Private data: generate_endpoints, get_account, get_service, list_plans, list_trusted_ips · Public sink: get_account, get_live_traffic · Destructive: generate_endpoints

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "generate_endpoints" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
